title: Shyama Devi v. State of U.P.
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed without merits; petitioner relegated to Para 6.8 objection with eight-week stay of coercive recovery.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash a recovery citation of Rs. 3,09,300 was disposed without examining merits. On the distribution licensee's statement, the High Court granted liberty to file an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks, to be decided after hearing within the next four weeks, and stayed coercive action for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever was earlier.
facts: Shyama Devi petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash a recovery citation dated 5 May 2022 issued by respondent no. 3 for Rs. 3,09,300 plus other charges, and to restrain further recovery. Counsel for respondent no. 4, the Power Distribution Corporation, stated on instructions that the petitioner could file an objection to the impugned demand, which would be decided in accordance with law within a time-bound period.

holding_units.topic: objection to demand as statutory alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation may be disposed without examining merits by granting liberty to submit an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided in accordance with law after hearing, with a time-bound stay of coercive recovery pending that disposal.

principle_tags.application: Writ against a recovery citation disposed without merits; petitioner directed to file a Para 6.8 objection for time-bound reasoned disposal after hearing, with stay of coercive action.

not_decided.point: Merits of the recovery citation and demand of Rs. 3,09,300
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits of the petitioner's case.
